odn2395_check:
INDEPENDENT FINDING - the current mapping is CORRECT in both directions, but the ODN 2395 OLIGO RECORD IS CONTAMINATED. 

WHAT EACH PAPER SAYS. (a) Lundberg Slingsby 2022, Methods 'Antisense oligonucleotides': 'Five ASO (all with a PS backbone) were included: three with 2'MOE sequences; 487660, 104838, 501861 and two with CpG sequences; 120704 and ODN 2395'. Its Table 1 - which I read as text from page 3 of the publisher PDF - lists the compound as '818290 (ODN 2395)', backbone 'CpG PS', length 22, PS load 21, and prints the sequence with a thioate star on every linkage; the footnote states '818290 is ODN 2395 and is referred to as ODN 2395 in the paper, for ease of comparison to previous reports.' So in source (a) 'ODN 2395' is unambiguously the FULLY PHOSPHOROTHIOATE 22-mer, i.e. Sewing's ODN2395_Thio. (b) Sewing 2017, Methods 'Oligonucleotides': 'we synthesized, ODN2395 Thio (+PS backbone) and ODN2395 (-PS backbone) as assay controls' and 'All tested molecules ... were all fully phosphorothiotated (PS) except ODN2395 (phosphodiester linkages)'. Table 2 prints ODN2395_Thio with stars on every linkage and bare ODN2395 with none. So in source (b) the bare name uniquely means the PHOSPHODIESTER variant. 

IS THE DATASET RIGHT? YES, and I verified it functionally rather than by name. All 38 Haematologica CpG-ODN rows point at TOLG184 (ODN2395_Thio, full_PS, ps_count 21); ZERO Haematologica rows point at TOLG183. On the Sewing side, TOLG183 ('ODN 2395', full_PO, ps_count 0) carries exactly the 6 rows whose values I re-derived from the workbook's '- PS' columns - PAC-1 1.652, P-selectin 2.745, GPVI 0.246, PF4-KKO 12.386, IL-8 0.78 - i.e. the inactive control. TOLG184 carries the 10 rows re-derived from the '+ PS' columns - PAC-1 18.935, P-selectin 9.653, GPVI 14.98, PF4-KKO 92.868, IL-8 25.0, MCP-1 53.56 - i.e. the strongly active reagent. The headline PS-drives-platelet-activation result is therefore NOT inverted. 

THE REMAINING DEFECT (in oligos.csv, outside the measurement slice but directly on this predictor). TOLG183 is the phosphodiester record (backbone_chemistry=full_PO, ps_count=0) yet it still carries the PS form's identity metadata merged in from source (a): aliases 'ISIS 818290;818290;PS-ODN 2395', a design_source list that includes '10.3324/haematol.2020.260059 Table 1', and notes asserting '22-mer with 21 PS linkages = full PS. GPVI KD 0.4 uM' - flatly contradicting its own ps_count=0 - alongside a stale fragment saying PS count was 'left TBD'. Any consumer resolving by alias would map ISIS 818290 (the PS reagent) onto the PO record and get the central predictor exactly backwards. The measurement-level remap was done; the oligo-level split was not finished. Recommended fix: strip 'ISIS 818290', '818290' and 'PS-ODN 2395' from TOLG183.aliases (they belong on TOLG184), drop the Haematologica Table 1 entry from TOLG183.design_source, and delete the '21 PS linkages / full PS / GPVI KD 0.4 uM' sentence and the 'commonly full-PS' fragment from TOLG183.notes. This is the most serious problem I found in or adjacent to this slice.
summary:
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION of the 272 in-vitro human-platelet rows (157 Lundberg Slingsby 2022 Haematologica; 115 Sewing 2017 PLoS One). Both sources were retrieved LIVE this session and re-read independently of the extraction: Europe PMC fullTextXML for both; the publisher PDF for the Haematologica article (PyMuPDF); the Haematologica supplementary appendix PDF; and, decisively, the Sewing S1 raw-data workbook (pone.0187574.s001.xlsx, 6 sheets) obtained from the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint. VERDICT: 246 CONFIRMED, 26 CORRECTED, 0 REJECTED. I found no fabricated value and no value attached to a locus that does not contain it - the failure mode I was most looking for. 

HOW THE NUMBERS WERE CHECKED. All 115 Sewing rows carry numeric values; I recomputed mean/SD/n from the raw per-replicate workbook cells for every one, and every stored value reproduces EXACTLY (e.g. TMSR001 (AC)10 PAC-1 18.169+/-3.623 n=5 from the '20' row of sheet 'Figure 1'; TMSR1181 ODN2395_Thio 18.935+/-4.294 from the '+ PS' row; TMSR1139 ODN2395 non-PS GPVI 0.246+/-0.239 n=12 from the '- PS' row). Of the 157 Haematologica rows, 39 carry numbers; all 39 were matched to the source - the Fig 1A/1B/3A/4D/4E/4F/7A proplatelet, P-selectin, aggregation and aggregate percentages to the exact Results sentences, the four Fig 3C/3D Pearson r values to the enumerated Results sentence, and the four Fig 7E Pearson r values plus the ten KD values to high-resolution renders of the Fig 7E plot, the Fig 7F 'Affinity to GPVI' inset table (487660 1.4, 104838 1.2, 501861 1.5, 120704 0.2, ODN 2395 0.4 uM) and the Supplementary Fig S5 'Affinity to Human Serum Albumin' inset table (12.9, 24, 26, 0.4, 2.5 uM). The remaining 118 Haematologica rows are qualitative (readout_value=TBD) and each was matched to a Results/legend sentence for that panel and compound. 

UNITS. Clean. Every row in the slice reads uM (105 at 5 uM, 22 at 1, 20 at 10 for Haematologica; 0.1-100 uM for Sewing). ZERO rows read mM. I reproduced the symbol-font artefact myself - the publisher PDF text layer renders '5 mM ASO' and 'HEPES, 10 mM' on pages 3-6 where the XML correctly reads uM - and confirmed the extraction used the XML. The only legitimate mM in either paper (Sewing's 10 mM PBS stock) was correctly not turned into a measurement row. 

A RECORDED CAVEAT I MUST REFUTE. I was told Table 1 of the Haematologica paper is 'a BITMAP in both XML and PDF, so sequences from it must be TBD'. Half right. It IS a bitmap in the Europe PMC XML (<table-wrap> contains only <graphic xlink:href='107519.tab1.jpg'>, no <table> element). It is NOT a bitmap in the publisher PDF: PyMuPDF extracts the whole table as text from page 3, including all five sequences, the backbone/length/PS-load columns and the footnotes. The dataset's own oligos.csv notes already say this ('Sequence IS text-extractable from Table 1 p3 of the Europe PMC PDF render'), so the extraction detected it correctly and the caveat handed to me is what is wrong. Sequences were nonetheless withheld as TBD - correctly, but for a LICENCE reason (CC BY-NC), not a retrievability one. 

SEQUENCES: NOTHING INVENTED. TOLG125 (487660), TOLG128 (501861) and TOLG035 (120704) all carry sequence_5to3=TBD. The derived chemistry attributed to Table 1 is verifiable and correct against the real table: 487660 2'MOE PS / 20 / 19, 104838 2'MOE PS / 20 / 19, 501861 2'MOE PS / 20 / 19, 120704 CpG PS / 24 / 23, 818290 (ODN 2395) CpG PS / 22 / 21, footnote 'All cytosine residues were methylated at the five position'. The 5-10-5 MOE motifs are visible in the MOE-annotated sequences. TOLG032's stored sequence GCTGATTAGAGAGAGGTCCC matches Table 1's 104838 entry character for character. TOLG183/184's TCGTCGTTTTCGGCGCGCGCCG matches BOTH Sewing Table 2 (a real parsed table, CC-BY) and Haematologica Table 1. No sequence in this slice is fabricated. 

LICENCES verified from the articles' own licence fields via Europe PMC: PMC8804562 = 'cc by-nc' (so redistribution=summary_stat on all 157 rows is correct and cc_by would have been an error); PMC5673186 = 'cc by' (so cc_by on all 115 rows is correct). 

CONTROLLED VOCABULARY: fully legal. study_type, species, delivery_method, dose_or_conc_unit, readout_category, effect_direction, tissue, redistribution and thrombocytopenia_grade contain no out-of-enum value anywhere in the 272. No duplicate measurement_id and no duplicate (oligo, locus, concentration, readout) key. 

TWO INDEPENDENT DATA-QUALITY CATCHES BY THE EXTRACTION THAT I CONFIRMED. (1) The S1 workbook's Fig 1C concentration labels (30/10/3/1/0.3 uM) are wrong - they run backwards against the response. The published Fig 1C x-axis is 0.1-10 uM. I rendered Fig 1C from the PLOS PDF at 900 dpi: the five plotted points sit at 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with PAC-1 SI ~1.0/1.02/1.55/3.05/4.35, which is exactly the dataset's assignment. The extraction relabelled correctly and disclosed it in notes. (2) The S1 'Figure 5' sheet's (C) GPVI block mislabels two rows ('AC9' twice, 'AC10 LNA' twice); the dataset reassigns them against the Fig 5C image and says so in notes. Both calls are right. 

GRADING. The concentration-relative rubric is applied consistently: activation at 5-10 uM -> grade 2; binding without aggregation -> grade 1; 50 uM cytokine release (which Sewing itself calls 'far in excess of clinically used doses') -> grade 1; explicit nulls -> grade 0. The four grade-3 rows are the only in-vitro 3s and all belong to (AC)8 at 1-3 uM. At 1 uM (TMSR051, TMSR056) that is rubric-correct (Haematologica gives Cmax 1-2 uM for 300 mg). At 3 uM (TMSR052, TMSR057) it is borderline - 3 uM is ~1.5-3x Cmax and grade 2 is an equally defensible reading; flagged per-row, not corrected, because the source supports either. 

OVERALL CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the Sewing half (every number re-derived from primary raw data - this is as strong as verification gets) and HIGH for the Haematologica half (every number matched to prose, an inset table, or a high-resolution figure render). The 26 corrections are flag/naming defects, not value errors. The most consequential problem I found is not in measurements.csv at all - see odn2395_check.
